title: Muslim Slave System in Medieval India
lede: In The Legacy of Muslim Rule in India Lal said slavery deserved a study of its own. This is that study. Drawing on the chronicles and on Islamic law (the Hidaya, the Hadis), he follows the system from war captives sent to the Caliph from Sindh, through the “Slave Sultans” who ruled Delhi, to the slave markets, the prices fixed by Alauddin Khalji, the soldiers and eunuchs, and the harem. His theme is that enslavement was tied to conversion. Captive women and children were raised as Muslims.

note: Slavery was common to many medieval societies, and historians debate its scale and character in India. Lal's account relies on chroniclers' figures, which can be inflated. This page summarises his findings, attributed to him, without his more graphic material.

sections.title: Slave prices under Alauddin Khalji's market controls
sections.lede: Alauddin (1296–1316) fixed the price of every commodity in Delhi's markets, slaves included. Barani lists slaves alongside horses and cattle. The bars show the top of each fixed range.
sections.note: Upper bound of each range as Lal gives it from Barani. Bulk buyers paid separate rates. Foreign slaves, usually Muslims, cost far more.
